findings.desc: dangling-cross-ref: §2.2 referenced but does not exist — §1.2 (line 17) and §1.3 (line 23) both cite §2.2 for the independence-test definition, but Section 2 has no numbered subsection 2.2; the independence test is defined under the unnumbered Step 2 heading. Reader directed to a non-existent anchor.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: both §2.2 citations (lines 17, 23) changed to '§2, Step 2', the actual heading where the independence test is defined.

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: docs/parallel-decomposition-spec.md §4.4 — evaluateDecompositionGate(story, peers, contracts, cfg) has no TypeScript types for `peers` or `contracts` parameters; an implementer reading the spec cannot write a type-safe call from canStartDevGuard. `peers` must be StoryInfo[] filtered from store; `contracts` must be Map<string,ScopeContractData|null> or similar — neither is stated. This gap forces guesswork or `as any` at the call site.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: evaluateDecompositionGate signature now typed — story: StoryInfo, peers: StoryInfo[], contracts: Map<string, ScopeContractData>, cfg: ParallelGateConfig; added a note that canStartDevGuard must load peers+contracts before the (pure) call.

findings.desc: dangling-cross-ref: §4.5 reference misleading — line 65 in Step 2 (Section 2) says "see §4.5 / §7-F4" for the point that actualFileOverlapsByStory() cannot produce meaningful results pre-DEV, but §4.5 (The one new schema field) covers schema field placement for depends/dependsMeta and says nothing about pre-DEV probe semantics. The only relevant material on this topic is in §4.2 and the F4 row in Section 7.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: line 65 cross-ref changed from '§4.5 / §7-F4' to '§4.2 / §7-F4' (§4.2 holds the pre-DEV probe semantics).

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: docs/parallel-decomposition-spec.md §4.4 line ~333 — self-contradictory catch-branch description for the new decomposition check inside canStartDevGuard. The text says the try/catch is "consistent with the guard's existing catch { return false } shape but inverted to fail-open". These two clauses contradict each other: the existing guard is fail-closed (return false); the new code must be fail-open (return true). An implementer following the first clause writes a fail-closed catch; following the second writes fail-open. Both cannot be true simultaneously. The correct intent (fail-open) must be stated unambiguously without the "consistent with" hedging, or the spec will produce incorrect implementations.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: reworded to state the new sub-check fails OPEN (returns true) — explicitly the opposite of the surrounding guard's fail-closed catch; removed the contradictory 'consistent with' hedging.

findings.desc: dangling-cross-ref: §4.4 says "fail-open, §4.7" but the fail-open/fail-closed policy is actually in §4.8 — line 333 in §4.4 writes "Wrap in try/catch returning true (fail-open, §4.7)" but §4.7 is the Config validation set section; the failure-mode guardrails including the fail-open rule are defined in §4.8. The §4.7 reference sends readers to the wrong section for the cited behavior.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: §4.4 fail-open reference corrected from §4.7 to §4.8 (failure-mode guardrails).

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: docs/parallel-decomposition-spec.md §4.2 / §4.3 — globsOverlap(a, b) return field `broad` is ambiguous. The function receives two write-sets; either or both could be broad. The spec says `broad: boolean` with no indication of whether it means (a is broad), (b is broad), or (a OR b is broad). Callers in evaluateDecompositionGate need to know which story has the broad glob to produce an actionable block message naming the colliding storyId. A single boolean loses this attribution. The parameter types for a and b are also not specified (presumably string[] from computeWriteSet but the spec omits them).
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: globsOverlap typed (a: string[], b: string[]) and broad:boolean replaced with broadSide: 'a'|'b'|'both'|null so §4.8 block messages can attribute the broad glob.

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: docs/parallel-decomposition-spec.md §4.7 — parallelGate nested object in AuditConfig is not type-safe under the existing readUserConfig pattern. The current code does `return parsed as Partial<AuditConfig>` and then validates each scalar field individually (e.g., VALID_MODES.has(userOverrides.mode as AuditMode)). Adding a nested `parallelGate: { mode, maxConcurrentReview, broadGlobBlocks }` object is NOT handled by this pattern: an implementer following the existing scalar approach would likely write `merged.parallelGate = userOverrides.parallelGate ?? profileDefaults.parallelGate` — which bypasses all per-field validation and allows invalid mode strings through without the promised console.warn+fallback. The spec says validation is "copied from deprecatedGcThreshold" but those are top-level scalars; no code sketch is given for validating the nested struct. This is a doc-promise-undelivered gap: the spec promises per-field validation semantics for the nested object but gives no implementation path that achieves it.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: added a dedicated resolveParallelGate(raw?: unknown) nested-object validation helper; documented that the per-scalar readUserConfig path does not recurse.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: spec §4.7 states VALID_MODES is typed to Set<AuditMode> but actual code in audit-config.ts declares it as ReadonlySet<AuditMode>. The logical conclusion (cannot be reused for parallelGate validation) is correct but the stated type annotation is factually wrong.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: VALID_MODES type corrected from Set<AuditMode> to ReadonlySet<AuditMode> (audit-config.ts:50).

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: all scope_boundary_set examples throughout the spec (§3.1, §3.2, §3.3, §5.1–5.4, §6, §8) omit the required userConfirmed parameter. The CLI schema (cli-engine.ts) declares userConfirmed: z.boolean() without .optional(), and the handler throws 'userConfirmed must be true before the INIT scope boundary can be saved' when absent. Any agent copying these templates verbatim will get a validation failure (safeParse exit code 1).
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: added required --userConfirmed=true to all four scope_boundary_set examples (§3.1, §3.2, §3.3, §5.1). Requirement verified against cli-engine.ts Zod schema (non-optional boolean).

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: all scope_contract_set examples in the spec (§3.1, §3.2, §3.3, §5.2, §5.3, §5.4, §6, §8) omit the required --mode parameter. The CLI schema (cli-engine.ts line 1976) declares mode: z.enum(['local','shadow','enforce']) without .optional() or .default(), so safeParse fails with 'Invalid enum value' when mode is absent. The handler defaults to 'enforce' (line 161 of scope-contract.ts), but that default is never reached because safeParse blocks first.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: added required --mode=enforce to all nine scope_contract_set examples (§3.1-3.3, §5.1-5.4, §6, §8). Requirement verified: cli-engine.ts:1976 mode enum is non-optional.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: spec §4.4 item 4 says 'handlers/lattice-parallel-wave.ts — resolveWaveSafety gains a scope_glob_overlap degradation kind'. However resolveWaveSafety is a non-exported private function in core/lattice-parallel-wave.ts (line 751), not in handlers/lattice-parallel-wave.ts. The handler file imports from core but does not expose resolveWaveSafety. A developer following the spec would edit the wrong file.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 76c535499: §4.4 item 4 corrected — resolveWaveSafety is a private function in core/lattice-parallel-wave.ts (line 751), not handlers/; reference and file path updated.

findings.desc: cfg.parallelGate.mode wrong field path at call site: §4.4 line 333 says canStartDevGuard checks `cfg.parallelGate.mode === block` after calling evaluateDecompositionGate(story, peers, contracts, cfg). But cfg is typed ParallelGateConfig (§4.4 line 341), which already IS the resolved nested object with fields {mode, maxConcurrentReview, broadGlobBlocks} — it has no .parallelGate sub-field. The correct check is `cfg.mode === block`. As written this is a runtime TypeError: any implementer copying this call site literally would access undefined and the block gate would silently never fire.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29bb434f7: §4.4 line 333 corrected to cfg.mode (cfg = resolveAuditConfig(...).parallelGate, a ParallelGateConfig); clarified the call site extracts parallelGate.

findings.desc: evaluateDecompositionGate mode-check responsibility is contradicted between §4.4 and §4.8: §4.4 (line 333) implies the gate always populates block regardless of mode, and the CALLER gates on cfg.mode=block. But §4.8 (line 389) says the gate itself checks mode internally for peer-unreadable: under mode=block the gate emits block, otherwise advisory. These are contradictory contracts: if the gate is mode-aware internally it should not emit block=null under advise mode, but the caller would still skip the block check. The spec must pick one authority (gate-decides-mode or caller-decides-mode) and apply it consistently to ALL block conditions including peer_contract_unreadable_parallel. As written an implementer cannot reconcile the two sections.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29bb434f7: resolved the §4.4-vs-§4.8 mode-check contradiction — the gate stays pure and only returns a block reason from scope facts; the cfg.mode check lives solely in the §4.4 caller. §4.8 peer-unreadable reworded to return the block reason, enforced by the caller under mode:block.

findings.desc: broadSide cross-reference points to wrong section: §4.4 line 340 says broadSide is for so §4.8 block messages can cite the offending story. §4.8 is the failure-mode guardrails section (fail-open/fail-closed, peer contract unreadable) — it contains no block-message formatting or broad-glob block messages. The broad_glob_unprovable_parallel block condition is defined in §4.3. The cross-reference should read §4.3, not §4.8. As written, an implementer reading the spec to understand how broadSide feeds block messages would be pointed at the wrong section.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29bb434f7: §4.4 broadSide cross-reference changed from §4.8 to the §4.3 broad_glob_unprovable_parallel block message.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: spec §3 intro bullet (line 147) shows `scope_boundary_set --storyId <id> --allowedScope <semantic dirs>` without the required `--userConfirmed=true` flag. The CLI schema (cli-engine.ts line 585) declares `userConfirmed: z.boolean()` without `.optional()`, so this command will fail validation if copied verbatim. The round-1 F-009 fix only patched the template-block examples (§3.1 line 181, §3.2 line 223, §3.3 line 256, §5.1 line 468) but left the first-exposure shorthand bullet in §3 incomplete. An implementer reading §3 before the templates sees the wrong signature.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29bb434f7: §3 intro shorthand bullet (line 147) now includes --userConfirmed=true on scope_boundary_set.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: spec §3 intro bullet (line 148) shows `scope_contract_set --storyId <id> --allowedModify … --allowedCreate … --allowedTest … --protectedFiles … --explicitExcludes …` without the required `--mode` parameter. The CLI schema (cli-engine.ts line 1976) declares `mode: z.enum(["local","shadow","enforce"])` without `.optional()` or `.default()`, so this command fails safeParse with an invalid-enum error when mode is absent. The round-1 F-010 fix only patched the template-block examples and the §5.1 meta-prompt bullet (line 469) but left the first-exposure shorthand in §3 (line 148) still missing `--mode`. An implementer who reads §3 to understand the command signature gets an incomplete model.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29bb434f7: §3 intro shorthand bullet (line 148) now includes --mode=enforce on scope_contract_set.

findings.desc: CHK-001: §4.4 line 333 still contains cfg.parallelGate.mode === "block" — but cfg in canStartDevGuard is ParallelGateConfig (the already-resolved nested object returned by resolveParallelGate), which has fields {mode, maxConcurrentReview, broadGlobBlocks} with NO .parallelGate sub-field. The correct access is cfg.mode === "block". As written this is a TypeError at runtime: the check always reads undefined, the block condition never fires, and the gate is silently disabled regardless of config. This was filed as F-012 in round 1 and remains unresolved in commit 76c535499.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29bb434f7: duplicate of F-012 — cfg.parallelGate.mode corrected to cfg.mode at §4.4 line 333.

findings.desc: CHK-002: §3.1, §3.2, §3.3 and §6 "Persist to Lattice" blocks show space-separated multiple values after a single array flag (e.g. --protectedFiles "contract.ts" "types.ts" "index.ts"). The CLI parser (cli-engine.ts parseFlags) only consumes ONE non-flag argument per flag invocation; the second and subsequent values are silently dropped as unrecognized positionals. In §3.2 (impl story) this means only contract.ts is added to protectedFiles, leaving types.ts and index.ts unprotected. In §3.1/§3.3 the allowedModify and allowedCreate lists are similarly truncated. Additionally §6 line 621 uses literal "<same>" as the --allowedCreate value — not a valid path. Correct form is either repeated flags (--protectedFiles f1 --protectedFiles f2) or JSON array (--protectedFiles ["f1","f2"]).

CHK-002: §4.4 vs §4.8 still contradict who is responsible for mode-checking. §4.4 (line 333) states the CALLER (canStartDevGuard) checks cfg.mode === block after evaluateDecompositionGate returns a non-null block — implying the gate always populates block regardless of mode. §4.8 (line 389) states the GATE itself checks mode internally: "under mode: block, refuse the parallel assertion (block with peer_contract_unreadable_parallel)". These two designs are irreconcilable: if the gate is mode-aware it should return block=null under advise mode, defeating the caller check; if the caller is mode-aware, the gate must always emit block strings and never check mode internally. An implementer cannot correctly implement evaluateDecompositionGate from this spec. Filed as F-013 in round 1, unresolved in commit 76c535499.

CHK-002: §4.4 line 340 says broadSide is for "§4.8 block messages" to cite the offending story, but §4.8 (failure-mode guardrails: fail-open/fail-closed, unreadable peer) contains no block-message formatting. The broad_glob_unprovable_parallel block condition is defined in §4.3. The cross-reference should read §4.3, not §4.8. Filed as F-014 in round 1, unresolved in commit 76c535499.
